correctness.rationale: Starting from Chen's exact quotient-distance formula, the identity factor converts each registered row comparison to the angle between a coordinate vector and a unit vector in a common rank-s subspace. Orthogonal projection gives the sharp coordinatewise bound by sqrt(P_ii). The function arccos^2(sqrt(p)) is proved strictly convex by an explicit second derivative whose numerator has positive derivative. Jensen then gives the sharp rank bound. Real Schur-Horn produces the constant-diagonal projection attaining it. Equality in Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz gives the complete minimizer set, and the corank-one specialization gives exactly the signed regular-simplex matrices.

value.rationale: Rank is the source's orbit stratification, and distance computation is a central problem for the proposed geometry. The theorem gives a closed form for the distance from the canonical full-rank point to every lower-rank stratum, despite the source's general lack of a closed form, and classifies every optimizer. The corank-one case gives an exact metric clearance to rank loss and identifies all nearest singular correlations. This is a structural all-dimensions result tied directly to the motivating metric, not an arbitrary finite slice or a reformulation of the quadratic Welch bound.
